blockers.title: Target SIGN ACL admits ANY and unknown authorizations before adding codesign
blockers.trigger: The one otherwise-valid finite nonempty target ACL has numeric authorizations [SIGN, ANY] or [SIGN, unrecognized-tag]. Owner, keychain, identity and application-count checks pass. This is an actual permitted input shape in the new C mutation path; it is not an assertion this shape occurred in the earlier Mac failure.
facts: inspectAccess treats ANY as known and only increments an aggregate unknownAuthorizationCount for an unknown tag. Neither state rejects a target SIGN ACL.
The append guard checks one SIGN ACL, finite list, no NULL or empty application list, and a list budget, but no target authorization policy.

SecACLSetContents appends the new real codesign subject while preserving the authorization group. SecKeychainItemSetAccess publishes it. Therefore the new subject receives ANY or unreviewed extra rights from that same ACL.

The Python summary accepts an unchanged positive unknownAuthorizationCount and exports no target-ANY fact, so its before/after count comparison does not reject this case. signAllowAnyACLCount counts a NULL application list, not the ANY authorization tag.

primaryEvidence.meaning: authorizes(right) accepts explicit right or ANY; ANY is a grant for every action.
SetContents preserves authorizations while replacing the application subject list; SetAuthorizations is a separate API.

blockers.minimalCorrection: While reading each numeric authorization group, track target-local hasANY and hasUnknown. Once isSign is known, reject either flag with a typed nonzero status before CopyContents/SetContents/SetAccess. Preserve unrelated unknown/opaque ACLs; a blanket aggregate unknown==0 is not equivalent. Leave known original limited rights and schema unchanged.
blockers.validationLimit: No C/Swift SDK or Keychain execution for this delta. Six existing portable methods exercise Python child/output/order boundaries and do not execute this native C policy.

reviewedInvariants.finding: Mutation is called only after the real reopened identity leaf/root and private-key public representation match. Native precheck reads the actual keychain, compares bounded file path bytes, queries exactly one private key in that one file and compares only public representations. These are scope/binding checks, not authority proofs.

The initial creator is added only to the one fresh SecAccess before its one existing PKCS12 import. A CHANGE_ACL tag alone is not trusted: exact public errSecInvalidOwnerEdit from unchanged-tag setter distinguishes owner, per pinned Apple implementation, before tag mutation. Unexpected status and ambiguous owner fail. This implementation-derived owner test still requires actual target-Mac evidence.

Original application objects, tags, prompt and unrelated entries remain in the access object; a current-platform codesign subject is appended once. Same-key access is persisted and copied afresh. Post-write normalized count comparison rejects unexpected reported changes. The target authorization rejection blocker above remains.

Existing CLI command is now constrained to private signing keys in the previously checked single owned file. A new importer process must inspect actual persisted partition plist and exactly one each apple-tool/apple/codesign with no other partition. No success inference from CLI exit alone.

Only fixed schema/operation/stage/counts/booleans and public certificate fingerprints are declassified; path/ACL/partition hex/password/raw private process output remain suppressed. Legacy schemas remain strict. Private-key challenge and path counts explicitly do not assert cross-process codesign ACL execution.

Public deprecated numeric ACL APIs, public Security status and C struct fields match the Swift use. No private SetAccessWithPassword declarations/calls, private key export, global search-list/trust edits or ad-hoc signature. This is a static finding, not compilation acceptance.
